title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook — Operations, Runbooks, Postmortems and Communications (Addendum)
author: Priya Raman
content:
Summary:

This addendum consolidates operational guidance, runbook maintenance best-practices, incident lifecycle templates, on-call rotation rules, game-day exercises, and customer/status-page communication templates for Redwood Inference’s on-call and incident response program. It is intended for engineers, on-call responders, incident commanders, product and customer success stakeholders.

Scope:
- Production services (hosted API, routing, model-serving runtime, Dedicated control plane)
- External-facing incidents (customer-impacting latency/errors) and internal reliability incidents that affect SLAs/SLOs

Objectives:
- Provide a single reference for triage, escalation, communications, and post-incident analysis
- Reduce time-to-detect and time-to-recover for Sev0/Sev1 incidents
- Standardize runbook ownership and maintenance cadence

Key definitions and severity matrix:
1) Severity levels (how to classify):
   - Sev0 (P0): Total outage or critical degradation causing >50% of customers to be unable to use core functionality (e.g., API returns 500 for all requests). Target: page within 2 minutes.
   - Sev1 (P1): Major degradation impacting a subset of traffic or important customers (e.g., large bump in 5xxs or model-serving errors for specific model families). Target: page within 15 minutes.
   - Sev2 (P2): Partial degradation or non-critical feature regression (e.g., increased latency p95 but <2× SLO). Page or Slack alert; no immediate phone page.

Severity rules of thumb (measurable):
- API error rate: Sev1 if 5xxs > 5% sustained for 5 minutes or >10% for 1 minute; Sev0 if >50% sustained for 2 minutes.
- Latency: Sev1 if p95 > 2× SLO for 5 minutes; Sev0 if p95 > 5× SLO or p50/p95 both degraded and customers experience timeouts.
- Throughput/backpressure: Sev1 if sustained throttling causing customer requests to be queued beyond configured timeouts.

Roles and responsibilities (on-call roster):
- Primary Pager (Responder): First responder; triage alerts, run initial remediation steps.
- Incident Commander (IC): Leads the incident for severity >= Sev1, coordinates cross-team activity, owns timeline and public comms decisions.
- Scribe / Notes: Records timeline, decisions, mitigations, and actions in the incident channel and postmortem.
- Communications Lead: Drafts status page messages and external customer comms in coordination with CS/PR.
- Subject Matter Experts (SMEs): Model-serving, routing, infra, networking — paged as needed for escalations.
- Engineering Manager / On-call Director: Notified for Sev0 and high-impact Sev1 incidents.

Incident lifecycle (step-by-step):
1) Detect & Alert:
   - Alerts fire through PagerDuty with clear runbook links and playbook steps. Each alert must include: metric, threshold, time window, affected service, runbook link.
2) Triage (0–15 minutes):
   - Primary Pager acknowledges immediately.
   - Quickly confirm: Is it real? Scope? Blast radius? (services, regions, customers)
   - If Sev1/Sev0, escalate to IC and open incident channel (#inc-<short-id>-<service>).
3) Declare Incident and Assign Roles (15–30 minutes):
   - IC announces incident, severity, and names for Scribe and Comms.
4) Mitigation & Short-term Fix (15–120 minutes):
   - Follow relevant runbook steps (see Runbooks section).
   - Implement mitigations: routing fallbacks, model-variant failover, increase replica counts, snapshot/kick caches, disable non-essential features.
5) Stabilize & Verify (30–240 minutes):
   - Confirm recovery across affected customers and regions; monitor error/latency metrics for 3× sampling interval.
6) Communicate (ongoing):
   - Comms lead posts initial status page + internal update within 30 minutes for Sev1/Sev0. Regular cadence every 60 minutes until resolved. See templates below.
7) Post-incident actions (24–72 hours):
   - IC hands to owner for postmortem. Create postmortem within 72 hours (draft) and publish within 7 calendar days.

Runbooks (owned, canonical):
- Each alert must link to a single runbook: path pattern /runbooks/<service>-<alert>.
- Runbook sections: Summary, Impact, Preconditions, Observability (dashboards, queries), Immediate checks, Mitigation steps (ordered), Rollback steps, Post-incident remediation tasks, Owner, Last updated.
- Maintenance cadence: owners must review runbook quarterly and after any incident where the runbook was used.

Minimal runbook template (example):
-----
Title: API high 5xxs (model-serving)
Service: api-gateway / model-router
Owner: Carlos Mendes (eng-serving-runtime)
Last updated: 2026-01-12
Indicators: 5xx rate, surfaced logs: model-runtime exceptions, backend connection errors
Immediate checks:
  - Check PagerDuty alert context and run basic curl to /health and /v1/models
  - Check k8s pod statuses: kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=model-runtime
  - Confirm if model shards report OOM or high GPU mem: /metrics/gpu_utilization
Mitigation steps (ordered):
  1) Scale up model-runtime replicas: kubectl scale deploy/model-runtime --replicas=6
  2) Enable routing fallback to light-quantized model variant: redwoodctl routing set-fallback --service model-runtime --variant q4_0
  3) If OOM persists, cordon node and drain suspected node; inform infra team.
Rollback: revert routing fallback with redwoodctl routing set-fallback --service model-runtime --revert
Postmortem tasks: tune batch size, add slower-traffic sampling, increase autoscaler window
-----

Escalation policy and contact matrix:
- Pager escalation: primary -> secondary (15 minutes) -> manager (30 minutes) -> IC (if not assigned)
- Contact matrix example (short):
  - Service: model-runtime => primary: oncall-model-runtime, secondary: model-runtime-2, SME: Daniel Park, manager: Aisha Thompson
  - infra-gpu => primary: infra-oncall, SME: Rajiv Kapoor

SLOs / Alert thresholds (examples):
- API availability SLO: 99.95% monthly (error budget policies documented in /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets.json)
- Latency SLO: p95 < 500ms for small-requests; alert when p95 > 900ms for 5 minutes
- Throughput: alert when QPS drops >40% vs baseline with corresponding increase in 5xxs

Status page and customer comms templates (copy/edit):
- Initial status page (within 30 minutes for Sev1/Sev0):
-----
Title: Degraded API responses in <region> — Investigating
Impact: Customers may see increased 5xx errors or higher latency for text generation requests. Some requests may time out.
Time started: 2026-02-10 21:06 UTC
What we are doing: We have identified an increase in 5xxs from the model-serving cluster and are routing to fallback variants while we investigate.
Customer guidance: We recommend retrying requests or temporarily routing to a different region. No data loss is expected.
Next update: in 60 minutes or sooner when we have a mitigation.
-----
- Follow-up status (post mitigation):
-----
Title: Service partially restored — Monitoring
Impact: Error rate has decreased to baseline for 80% of traffic; we are continuing to monitor and run validation checks.
Time updated: 2026-02-10 22:08 UTC
What we changed: Enabled fallback routing to q4_0 variant and scaled model-runtime replicas; running validation prompts to confirm model outputs.
Next steps: Run a full reconciliation and publish postmortem within 7 days.
-----
- Customer email template (short):
Subject: Incident update: Degraded API responses (2026-02-10)
Body: Thank you for your patience. We experienced service degradation affecting text-generation requests in <region>. We have implemented a temporary fallback and most requests are now functioning. We are continuing validation and will share a postmortem. If you have critical concerns, reply to this message and our CS team will escalate.

Postmortem template (required fields):
- Title
- Incident ID / Severity
- Timeline (UTC) — bullet list of events with timestamps
- Impact (customers, regions, features)
- Root cause analysis (technical summary)
- Contributing factors
- Corrective actions (short-term and long-term) with owners and due dates
- Detection & response: What worked / what didn't
- Follow-up remediation plan and verification steps
- Lessons learned and prevention items
- Link to runbooks and logs used

On-call rotations and rules:
- Primary on-call shifts: 1-week rotations for infra and serving-runtime teams; 24/7 coverage via PagerDuty.
- Shift handover: Post a handover note at start/end of shift with outstanding alerts, on-going mitigations, and any maintenance windows.
- On-call time limits: max 2 consecutive weeks as primary unless pre-approved. Secondary on-call can be weekend-only with 1-week rotations.
- Coverage exceptions: Use the on-call calendar and request swaps via the oncall-admin Slack app; manager approval required for >1 week swaps.

Game days and exercises (quarterly):
- Objective: Validate runbooks, SLO alerting, cross-team communication, and incident comms.
- Cadence: Quarterly game day per service team; one tabletop + one live fault-injection scenario per year for high-risk services.
- Play structure:
  1) Pre-brief: Objectives, scope, safety checks (no production data deletion allowed), rollback plan.
  2) Inject: Trigger alert via synthetic traffic failure or chaos engineering tool for a controlled model-serving degradation.
  3) Respond: Run full incident lifecycle using real pager and incident channel.
  4) Debrief & action items: Produce a short game-day report and feed into runbook updates.

Runbook ownership and maintenance checklist:
- Owner listed and pager duty team mapped in header
- Last tested date and game-day history
- Observability queries and dashboards embedded
- Rollback and mitigation steps validated in staging quarterly
- Post-incident edits applied within 5 business days after incident

Quick operational commands & observability queries (examples):
- k8s: kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=model-runtime | grep CrashLoopBackOff
- Logs: jq '.message' /var/log/model-runtime.log | tail -n 100
- Metric query (Prometheus): sum(rate(http_request_errors_total[5m])) by (service)
- Fallback routing (internal CLI): redwoodctl routing set-fallback --service model-runtime --variant q4_0 --reason "high-5xxs"

Appendix: Useful links and contact points:
- Incident channel naming: #inc-<short-id>-<service>
- PagerDuty escalation policy: internal link: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/pagerduty-escalation-policy.json
- SLO & error budget docs: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets.json
- Runbook folder: /runbooks/ (internal git-backed wiki)

Maintenance and governance:
- This document is maintained by the Eng SRE on-call program lead. Reviewers: eng-platform, eng-serving-runtime, customer-success.
- Review cadence: document review every 6 months; runbooks quarterly.

Contact for questions or feedback: priya.raman@redwood-inference.com
